prompt: Add retries to the job queue. jobqueue.py's Queue.fail(job_id, error) should count the failure in the job's attempts and put it back to run again at now + base * 2**(attempts-1) seconds (now is the time the job was taken to run; base is Queue(base=...)), up to max_attempts (the job's own, else the queue's default); when a failure reaches it the job is dead: it leaves the queue for queue.dead_letters with its last error. Queue.next(now) must return the ready job with the earliest due time (ties by job id), or None. worker.py's run_once(queue, handlers, now) takes the next job, calls handlers[job.kind](job.payload), and calls queue.done or queue.fail (with the exception's message) as the handler returns or raises; a job whose kind has no handler is dead at once with error "no handler". stats.py's summary(queue, now) must return a dict of pending (jobs still in the queue), waiting (of those, due later than now), dead and done counts.
